name: Zebadiah
overview: Zebadiah is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Shephatiah and the son of Michael. He is noted for his association with the group that returned to Jerusalem with Ezra, highlighting his role in the post-exilic restoration period. No tribal affiliation or additional notes are provided in Scripture regarding his background.
namesAndTitles: The name Zebadiah means 'YHWH bestows,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's provision. This proper name, recorded in Ezra 8:8, underscores the biblical pattern of names bearing spiritual significance but was not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Zebadiah is explicitly identified as the son of Michael in Scripture, as noted in Ezra 8:8. Beyond this paternal relationship and his descent from Shephatiah, no further family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zebadiah's significance lies in his participation among those who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra, marking him as part of the faithful remnant committed to restoring worship and community life after the Babylonian exile. His lineage from Shephatiah and connection to Michael situate him within the broader narrative of God's people reestablishing themselves under divine guidance. Although not extensively detailed, his presence in Ezra 8:8 contributes to the historical account of the returnees and their organization.
